title: Who the welfare state protects shapes a country’s financial openness
byline: Martino Comelli, Pedro Perfeito Da Silva
excerpt: Advanced economies did not simply abandon capital controls after the 1944 Bretton Woods Agreement. Martino Comelli and Pedro Perfeito Da Silva show that welfare states quietly took over their job. Countries that protect workers can afford open financial borders. Countries that spend mainly on pensioners still police the movement of money
content_html:
Advanced economies did not simply abandon capital controls after the 1944 Bretton Woods Agreement. Martino Comelli and Pedro Perfeito Da Silva show that welfare states quietly took over their job. Countries that protect workers can afford open financial borders. Countries that spend mainly on pensioners still police the movement of money

What Keynes called heresy

In 1944, defending the Bretton Woods plans in the House of Lords, John Maynard Keynes celebrated a conversion: 'the plan accords to every member Government the explicit right to control all capital movements. What used to be a heresy is now endorsed as orthodox'. Capital controls are rules that limit how money moves across borders, from taxes on foreign inflows to restrictions on taking money out of the country. The postwar financial order stayed on a national leash, and governments used this policy space to pursue full employment and build welfare states.

Development of the welfare state in Europe happened in a regime of tight capital controls. Welfare and capital controls grew together because they had similar goals. Every capitalist state must keep accumulation going while keeping society governable. Capital controls handled the external side, blocking the sudden flight of money that punishes governments and disciplines workers. Welfare handled the internal side, absorbing the people and risks the market discarded.

Most economies, decades into liberalisation, still restrict cross-border finance somehow

The 1970s broke the Bretton Woods system, closing the parenthesis of the Keynesian heresy, back to market orthodoxy. Washington ended dollar convertibility in 1971, finance went global, and the threat of exit became a permanent presence at every bargaining table, as capital chased lower wages and higher financial profits.

Yet capital controls never disappeared completely: IMF data compiled by Andres Fernández and colleagues show that most economies, decades into liberalisation, still restrict cross-border finance somehow. The interesting question is why some countries keep the drawbridge up while others let it down.

Not how much, but on whom

The standard answer, going back to Dani Rodrik, holds that open economies compensate their citizens. More exposure to world markets, more social spending.

Our new study in Social Policy & Administration finds that this compensation thesis misses the composition of that spending. We split the welfare budget into three. Passive spending covers pensions. Protective spending covers health, family and unemployment support for the working-age population. Productive spending covers training and education.

Across OECD countries from 1995 to 2019, the welfare mix correlates with the cross-border financial regime. Countries that tilt their budgets towards pensions maintain tighter capital controls. Countries that protect and train their workforce keep their financial borders open. Housing wealth pushes in the same direction, because households sitting on appreciating assets acquire a direct stake in open finance.

Open economies compensate their citizens: more exposure to world markets, more social spending. But how that money is spent is just as important

The mechanism behind the scenes is what Walter Korpi called the 'democratic class struggle' then crystallised in welfare arrangements. Protective spending gives workers back part of the bargaining power that mobile capital takes from them. Productive spending moves economies away from price competition, so governments no longer need to defend the exchange rate. Pensions, on the other hand, do neither: they secure people who have already left the labour market.

Four welfare-capital configurations

A cluster analysis sorts the OECD into recognisable families. Comprehensive welfare states, Nordic and Continental alike, pair broad social investment with the most open capital accounts. Post-communist industrial economies pair pension-heavy welfare with the tightest restrictions. Liberal economies stay open through large banking sectors and housing wealth rather than public protection. And countries with thin welfare across the board also keep controls, because nothing else cushions the blows.

Coverage beats generosity

We then widened the lens beyond the OECD with the Global Welfare Dataset, covering 35 countries including large emerging economies. There, the share of the population that social assistance can reach matters more than the money spent. Broad coverage travels with open capital accounts. Narrow coverage travels with controls, whatever the budget.

The cases behave as the numbers suggest. Poland directs roughly two thirds of its social spending to people outside the labour market and runs the tightest capital flow management in the Visegrád group. Uruguay built one of Latin America’s broadest welfare systems and has kept its capital account open since the 1990s. Chile, whose dictatorship privatised and segmented social protection, has repeatedly reached for capital controls to steady an exposed society.

Austerity breeds financial protectionism

The pattern invites us to read welfare as macroprudential policy, part of the toolkit that keeps financial openness politically survivable. Where redistribution runs vertically and broadly, the welfare state itself absorbs the shocks of global finance. Where it runs horizontally, protecting established insiders while the rest carry the risk, governments buy stability at the financial border instead. Capital controls work as a cheap, imperfect substitute for redistribution. They calm an exposed society without asking anyone at the top to pay.

Where redistribution runs vertically and broadly, the welfare state absorbs global finance shocks. Where it runs horizontally, governments buy stability at the financial border

Gut broad social protection, and you don't get a free market, you get working people and exposed businesses demanding that borders close. Keynes watched a heresy become orthodoxy because the old order had made itself unbearable after the crisis of 1929 and the fall of gold-standard liberalism. Analogously, regimes that dismantled the welfare that made openness bearable should not be surprised when the drawbridge starts rising again, as in Trump’s America and elsewhere, becoming a policy tool of the right.

The paper on which this blog piece is based won the ECPR Standing Group on Political Economy and Welfare State Politics Best Paper prize 2025

sentences.zh: 资本管制是一种廉价但不完美的再分配替代品。

sentences.en: They calm an exposed society without asking anyone at the top to pay.
sentences.zh: 他们平息了暴露的社会，却没有要求任何高层人士付费。

sentences.en: Where redistribution runs vertically and broadly, the welfare state absorbs global finance shocks.
sentences.zh: 当再分配纵向而广泛地进行时，福利国家就会吸收全球金融冲击。

sentences.en: Where it runs horizontally, governments buy stability at the financial border Gut broad social protection, and you don't get a free market, you get working people and exposed businesses demanding that borders close.
sentences.zh: 在横向运行的地方，政府在金融边界购买稳定，并提供广泛的社会保护，但你得不到自由市场，而是工薪阶层和暴露的企业要求关闭边界。

sentences.en: Keynes watched a heresy become orthodoxy because the old order had made itself unbearable after the crisis of 1929 and the fall of gold-standard liberalism.
sentences.zh: 凯恩斯眼睁睁地看着异端邪说变成正统，因为在 1929 年危机和金本位自由主义垮台之后，旧秩序已经变得难以忍受。

sentences.en: Analogously, regimes that dismantled the welfare that made openness bearable should not be surprised when the drawbridge starts rising again, as in Trump’s America and elsewhere, becoming a policy tool of the right.
sentences.zh: 类似地，当吊桥再次开始升起时，那些废除了使开放变得可以忍受的福利的政权，就像在特朗普领导下的美国和其他地方一样，成为右翼的政策工具，也不应该感到惊讶。

blocks.html_en: Advanced economies did not simply abandon capital controls after the 1944 Bretton Woods Agreement. Martino Comelli and Pedro Perfeito Da Silva show that welfare states quietly took over their job. Countries that protect workers can afford open financial borders. Countries that spend mainly on pensioners still police the movement of money

sentences.zh: 1944 年布雷顿森林协定签署后，发达经济体并没有简单地放弃资本管制。

sentences.en: Martino Comelli and Pedro Perfeito Da Silva show that welfare states quietly took over their job.
sentences.zh: 马蒂诺·科梅利和佩德罗·佩菲托·达席尔瓦表明，福利国家悄然接管了他们的工作。

sentences.en: Countries that protect workers can afford open financial borders.
sentences.zh: 保护工人的国家有能力开放金融边界。

sentences.en: Countries that spend mainly on pensioners still police the movement of money

blocks.html_en: What Keynes called heresy

sentences.en: What Keynes called heresy
sentences.zh: 凯恩斯所说的异端

blocks.html_en: In 1944, defending the Bretton Woods plans in the House of Lords, John Maynard Keynes celebrated a conversion: 'the plan accords to every member Government the explicit right to control all capital movements. What used to be a heresy is now endorsed as orthodox'. Capital controls are rules that limit how money moves across borders, from taxes on foreign inflows to restrictions on taking money out of the country. The postwar financial order stayed on a national leash, and governments used this policy space to pursue full employment and build welfare states.

sentences.en: In 1944, defending the Bretton Woods plans in the House of Lords, John Maynard Keynes celebrated a conversion: 'the plan accords to every member Government the explicit right to control all capital movements.
sentences.zh: 1944年，约翰·梅纳德·凯恩斯在上议院为布雷顿森林计划辩护时庆祝了这一转变：“该计划赋予每个政府成员国明确的控制所有资本流动的权利。”

sentences.en: What used to be a heresy is now endorsed as orthodox'.
sentences.zh: 曾经被视为异端的东西现在被认可为正统”。

sentences.en: Capital controls are rules that limit how money moves across borders, from taxes on foreign inflows to restrictions on taking money out of the country.
sentences.zh: 资本管制是限制资金跨境流动的规则，从对外资流入征税到限制资金出境。

sentences.en: The postwar financial order stayed on a national leash, and governments used this policy space to pursue full employment and build welfare states.
sentences.zh: 战后的金融秩序仍然受到国家的约束，各国政府利用这一政策空间来追求充分就业和建立福利国家。

blocks.html_en: Development of the welfare state in Europe happened in a regime of tight capital controls. Welfare and capital controls grew together because they had similar goals. Every capitalist state must keep accumulation going while keeping society governable. Capital controls handled the external side, blocking the sudden flight of money that punishes governments and disciplines workers. Welfare handled the internal side, absorbing the people and risks the market discarded.

sentences.en: Development of the welfare state in Europe happened in a regime of tight capital controls.
sentences.zh: 欧洲福利国家的发展发生在严格的资本管制制度下。

sentences.en: Welfare and capital controls grew together because they had similar goals.
sentences.zh: 福利和资本管制一起发展，因为它们有相似的目标。

sentences.en: Every capitalist state must keep accumulation going while keeping society governable.
sentences.zh: 每个资本主义国家都必须保持积累，同时保持社会的治理。

sentences.en: Capital controls handled the external side, blocking the sudden flight of money that punishes governments and disciplines workers.
sentences.zh: 资本管制控制外部，阻止资金突然外逃，从而惩罚政府和纪律工人。

sentences.en: Welfare handled the internal side, absorbing the people and risks the market discarded.
sentences.zh: 福利处理在内部，吸纳了群众，风险则被市场抛弃。

sentences.zh: 大多数经济体在经历自由化几十年后，仍然以某种方式限制跨境金融

blocks.html_en: The 1970s broke the Bretton Woods system, closing the parenthesis of the Keynesian heresy, back to market orthodoxy. Washington ended dollar convertibility in 1971, finance went global, and the threat of exit became a permanent presence at every bargaining table, as capital chased lower wages and higher financial profits.

sentences.en: The 1970s broke the Bretton Woods system, closing the parenthesis of the Keynesian heresy, back to market orthodoxy.
sentences.zh: 20 世纪 70 年代打破了布雷顿森林体系，结束了凯恩斯主义异端的括号，回到了市场正统观念。

sentences.en: Washington ended dollar convertibility in 1971, finance went global, and the threat of exit became a permanent presence at every bargaining table, as capital chased lower wages and higher financial profits.
sentences.zh: 1971年，华盛顿终止了美元兑换，金融走向全球，随着资本追逐更低的工资和更高的财务利润，退出的威胁成为每个谈判桌上永久存在的威胁。

blocks.html_en: Yet capital controls never disappeared completely: IMF data compiled by Andres Fernández and colleagues show that most economies, decades into liberalisation, still restrict cross-border finance somehow. The interesting question is why some countries keep the drawbridge up while others let it down.

sentences.en: Yet capital controls never disappeared completely: IMF data compiled by Andres Fernández and colleagues show that most economies, decades into liberalisation, still restrict cross-border finance somehow.
sentences.zh: 然而资本管制从未完全消失：安德烈斯·费尔南德斯及其同事编制的国际货币基金组织数据显示，大多数经济体在经历自由化几十年后，仍然以某种方式限制跨境金融。

sentences.en: The interesting question is why some countries keep the drawbridge up while others let it down.
sentences.zh: 有趣的问题是，为什么有些国家保持吊桥升起，而另一些国家则放下。

blocks.html_en: Our new study in Social Policy & Administration finds that this compensation thesis misses the composition of that spending. We split the welfare budget into three. Passive spending covers pensions. Protective spending covers health, family and unemployment support for the working-age population. Productive spending covers training and education.

sentences.en: Our new study in Social Policy & Administration finds that this compensation thesis misses the composition of that spending.
sentences.zh: 我们在《社会政策与管理》中的新研究发现，这一薪酬论文忽略了该支出的构成。

sentences.en: We split the welfare budget into three.
sentences.zh: 我们将福利预算一分为三。

sentences.en: Passive spending covers pensions.
sentences.zh: 被动支出包括养老金。

sentences.en: Protective spending covers health, family and unemployment support for the working-age population.
sentences.zh: 保护性支出涵盖对工作年龄人口的健康、家庭和失业支持。

sentences.en: Productive spending covers training and education.
sentences.zh: 生产性支出包括培训和教育。

blocks.html_en: Across OECD countries from 1995 to 2019, the welfare mix correlates with the cross-border financial regime. Countries that tilt their budgets towards pensions maintain tighter capital controls. Countries that protect and train their workforce keep their financial borders open. Housing wealth pushes in the same direction, because households sitting on appreciating assets acquire a direct stake in open finance.

sentences.en: Across OECD countries from 1995 to 2019, the welfare mix correlates with the cross-border financial regime.
sentences.zh: 从 1995 年到 2019 年，经合组织国家的福利结构与跨境金融制度相关。

sentences.en: Countries that tilt their budgets towards pensions maintain tighter capital controls.
sentences.zh: 将预算向养老金倾斜的国家保持更严格的资本管制。

sentences.en: Countries that protect and train their workforce keep their financial borders open.
sentences.zh: 保护和培训劳动力的国家保持金融边界开放。

sentences.en: Housing wealth pushes in the same direction, because households sitting on appreciating assets acquire a direct stake in open finance.
sentences.zh: 住房财富向同一方向推动，因为拥有升值资产的家庭获得了开放金融的直接股份。

sentences.en: But how that money is spent is just as important

blocks.html_en: The mechanism behind the scenes is what Walter Korpi called the 'democratic class struggle' then crystallised in welfare arrangements. Protective spending gives workers back part of the bargaining power that mobile capital takes from them. Productive spending moves economies away from price competition, so governments no longer need to defend the exchange rate. Pensions, on the other hand, do neither: they secure people who have already left the labour market.

sentences.zh: 幕后机制就是沃尔特·科尔皮（Walter Korpi）所说的“民主阶级斗争”，然后在福利安排中具体化。

sentences.en: Protective spending gives workers back part of the bargaining power that mobile capital takes from them.
sentences.zh: 保护性支出让工人恢复了流动资本从他们手中夺走的部分议价能力。

sentences.en: Productive spending moves economies away from price competition, so governments no longer need to defend the exchange rate.
sentences.zh: 生产性支出使经济摆脱价格竞争，因此政府不再需要捍卫汇率。

sentences.en: Pensions, on the other hand, do neither: they secure people who have already left the labour market.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，养老金则两者都没有：它们保护已经离开劳动力市场的人。

blocks.html_en: A cluster analysis sorts the OECD into recognisable families. Comprehensive welfare states, Nordic and Continental alike, pair broad social investment with the most open capital accounts. Post-communist industrial economies pair pension-heavy welfare with the tightest restrictions. Liberal economies stay open through large banking sectors and housing wealth rather than public protection. And countries with thin welfare across the board also keep controls, because nothing else cushions the blows.

sentences.en: A cluster analysis sorts the OECD into recognisable families.
sentences.zh: 聚类分析将经合组织分为可识别的家族。

sentences.zh: 北欧和大陆等全面福利国家都将广泛的社会投资与最开放的资本账户结合起来。

sentences.en: Post-communist industrial economies pair pension-heavy welfare with the tightest restrictions.
sentences.zh: 后共产主义工业经济体将大量养老金福利与最严格的限制结合起来。

sentences.en: Liberal economies stay open through large banking sectors and housing wealth rather than public protection.
sentences.zh: 自由经济体通过大型银行业和住房财富而不是公共保护来保持开放。

sentences.en: And countries with thin welfare across the board also keep controls, because nothing else cushions the blows.
sentences.zh: 福利全面薄弱的国家也会保持控制，因为没有其他办法可以缓解打击。

blocks.html_en: We then widened the lens beyond the OECD with the Global Welfare Dataset, covering 35 countries including large emerging economies. There, the share of the population that social assistance can reach matters more than the money spent. Broad coverage travels with open capital accounts. Narrow coverage travels with controls, whatever the budget.

blocks.html_en: The cases behave as the numbers suggest. Poland directs roughly two thirds of its social spending to people outside the labour market and runs the tightest capital flow management in the Visegrád group. Uruguay built one of Latin America’s broadest welfare systems and has kept its capital account open since the 1990s. Chile, whose dictatorship privatised and segmented social protection, has repeatedly reached for capital controls to steady an exposed society.

1944 年布雷顿森林协定签署后，发达经济体并没有简单地放弃资本管制。 马蒂诺·科梅利和佩德罗·佩菲托·达席尔瓦表明，福利国家悄然接管了他们的工作。 保护工人的国家有能力开放金融边界。 主要花钱在养老金领取者身上的国家仍在监管资金流动 凯恩斯称之为异端 1944 年，约翰·梅纳德·凯恩斯在上议院为布雷顿森林计划辩护时，庆祝了这一转变：“该计划赋予每个成员国政府控制所有资本流动的明确权利。” 曾经被视为异端的东西现在被认可为正统”。 资本管制是限制资金跨境流动的规则，从对外资流入征税到限制资金出境。 战后的金融秩序仍然受到国家的约束，各国政府利用这一政策空间来追求充分就业和建立福利国家。 欧洲福利国家的发展发生在严格的资本管制制度下。 福利和资本管制一起发展，因为它们有相似的目标。 每个资本主义国家都必须保持积累，同时保持社会的治理。 资本管制控制外部，阻止资金突然外逃，从而惩罚政府和纪律工人。 福利处理在内部，吸纳了群众，风险则被市场抛弃。 大多数经济体在经历了自由化几十年后，仍然以某种方式限制跨境金融。20世纪70年代打破了布雷顿森林体系，结束了凯恩斯异端邪说，回到了市场正统观念。 1971年，华盛顿终止了美元兑换，金融走向全球，随着资本追逐更低的工资和更高的财务利润，退出的威胁成为每个谈判桌上永久存在的威胁。 然而资本管制从未完全消失：安德烈斯·费尔南德斯及其同事编制的国际货币基金组织数据显示，大多数经济体在经历自由化几十年后，仍然以某种方式限制跨境金融。 有趣的问题是，为什么有些国家保持吊桥升起，而另一些国家则放下。 不是多少，而是谁。标准答案可以追溯到丹尼·罗德里克（Dani Rodrik），认为开放经济体会补偿其公民。 更多地接触世界市场，更多的社会支出。 社会援助支出的资本管制（CCI）（GLOW 数据库）。 2001-2019 年国家级平均水平 我们在《社会政策与管理》中的新研究发现，该补偿论文忽略了该支出的构成。 我们将福利预算一分为三。 被动支出包括养老金。 保护性支出涵盖对工作年龄人口的健康、家庭和失业支持。 生产性支出包括培训和教育。 从 1995 年到 2019 年，经合组织国家的福利结构与跨境金融制度相关。 将预算向养老金倾斜的国家保持更严格的资本管制。 保护和培训劳动力的国家保持金融边界开放。 住房财富向同一方向推动，因为拥有升值资产的家庭获得了开放金融的直接股份。 开放经济体补偿其公民：更多地接触世界市场、更多的社会支出。 但这些钱如何花掉也同样重要。幕后机制就是沃尔特·科尔皮（Walter Korpi）所说的“民主阶级斗争”，然后在福利安排中具体化。 保护性支出让工人恢复了流动资本从他们手中夺走的部分议价能力。 生产性支出使经济摆脱价格竞争，因此政府不再需要捍卫汇率。 另一方面，养老金则两者都没有：它们保护已经离开劳动力市场的人。 四种福利资本配置 聚类分析将经合组织分为可识别的家族。 北欧和大陆等全面福利国家都将广泛的社会投资与最开放的资本账户结合起来。 后共产主义工业经济体将大量养老金福利与最严格的限制结合起来。 自由经济体通过大型银行业和住房财富而不是公共保护来保持开放。 福利全面薄弱的国家也会保持控制，因为没有其他办法可以缓解打击。 沃德国家集群及其标准化维度 覆盖范围胜过慷慨 然后我们利用全球福利数据集将视角扩大到经合组织以外，覆盖包括大型新兴经济体在内的 35 个国家。 在那里，社会援助能够覆盖到的人口比例比所花的钱更重要。 广泛的覆盖范围与开放的资本账户一起旅行。 无论预算如何，狭窄的覆盖范围都会受到控制。 这些案例的表现正如数字所示。 波兰将大约三分之二的社会支出用于劳动力市场以外的人，并在维谢格拉德集团中实行最严格的资本流动管理。 乌拉圭建立了拉丁美洲最广泛的福利体系之一，并自 20 世纪 90 年代以来一直保持资本账户开放。 智利的独裁统治将社会保障私有化和分割，一再实施资本管制，以稳定暴露的社会。 紧缩滋生金融保护主义 这种模式让我们将福利解读为宏观审慎政策，它是保持金融开放在政治上生存的工具包的一部分。 当再分配纵向而广泛地进行时，福利国家本身就会吸收全球金融的冲击。 如果它是横向运行的，保护既定的内部人士，而其他人则承担风险，政府反而会在金融边界购买稳定。 资本管制是一种廉价但不完美的再分配替代品。 他们平息了暴露的社会，却没有要求任何高层人士付费。 当再分配纵向而广泛地进行时，福利国家就会吸收全球金融冲击。 在横向运行的地方，政府在金融边界购买稳定，并提供广泛的社会保护，但你得不到自由市场，而是工薪阶层和暴露的企业要求关闭边界。 凯恩斯眼睁睁地看着异端邪说变成正统，因为在 1929 年危机和金本位自由主义垮台之后，旧秩序已经变得难以忍受。 类似地，当吊桥再次开始升起时，那些废除了使开放变得可以忍受的福利的政权，就像在特朗普领导下的美国和其他地方一样，成为右翼的政策工具，也不应该感到惊讶。
